/-!
# Conjecture 8.16

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

Is the class of all $\overline{Z}$-groups closed under taking normal subgroups?

The class of $\overline{Z}$-groups is one of Kurosh's classes of generalized nilpotent
groups, defined via systems of subgroups. A *system* of subgroups of a group $G$ is a set
of subgroups of $G$ that contains $E$ and $G$, is linearly ordered by inclusion, and is
complete (closed under unions and intersections of its subfamilies). A *jump* of the system
is a pair $A \subset B$ of members with no member strictly between them; $B/A$ is the
corresponding *factor* of the system. A system is *invariant* if all of its members are
normal in $G$, and it is *central* if it is invariant and every factor $B/A$ is central,
i.e. $B/A \subseteq Z(G/A)$, equivalently $[B, G] \subseteq A$. A system $\mathfrak{B}$
*refines* a system $\mathfrak{A}$ if $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{B}$.

A group $G$ is a *$Z$-group* if it possesses a central system, and a *$\overline{Z}$-group*
if every invariant system of $G$ can be refined to a central system of $G$. Groups with an
ascending central series ($ZA$-groups, i.e. hypercentral groups) are $\overline{Z}$-groups,
and $\overline{Z}$-groups are $Z$-groups. Kurosh's $Z$-groups are unrelated to Mathlib's
`IsZGroup` (finite groups with cyclic Sylow subgroups).

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 8.16
* A. G. Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, Vol. II, Chapter XV, § 62 (Generalized nilpotent
  groups); the notions of normal, invariant and central systems and their refinements are
  introduced in Chapter XIV, § 56.
-/

structure IsCentralSystem (𝒜 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop
    extends IsInvariantSystem 𝒜 where
  central : ∀ A B, IsJump 𝒜 A B → ⁅B, (⊤ : Subgroup G)⁆ ≤ A
blocks.docstring:
A *central system* of a group $G$ (Kurosh): an invariant system all of whose factors are
central, i.e. for every jump $A \subset B$ the factor $B/A$ lies in the centre of $G/A$,
equivalently $[B, G] \subseteq A$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.16».IsCentralSystem
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's central system: invariant system all of whose factors B/A are central in G/A ([B,G] ≤ A).

/-- A group $G$ is a *$\overline{Z}$-group* (Kurosh) if every invariant system of $G$ can be

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isInvariantSystem_pair : IsInvariantSystem ({⊥, ⊤} : Set (Subgroup G)) where
  normal A hA := by
    rcases hA with rfl | rfl <;> infer_instance
  bot_mem := by simp
  top_mem := by simp
  isChain := IsChain.pair bot_le
  sSup_mem S hS _ := by
    by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ S
    · simp [top_unique (le_sSup h)]
    · have : sSup S = ⊥ := sSup_eq_bot.mpr fun a ha => by
        rcases hS ha with rfl | rfl
        · rfl
        · exact absurd ha h
      simp [this]
  sInf_mem S hS _ := by
    by_cases h : ⊥ ∈ S
    · simp [bot_unique (sInf_le h)]
    · have : sInf S = ⊤ := sInf_eq_top.mpr fun a ha => by
        rcases hS ha with rfl | rfl
        · exact absurd ha h
        · rfl
      simp [this]

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question: the Prop is ∀ G [Group G], G is a Z̄-group → ∀ N ⊴ G, N is a Z̄-group (to be stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` with all quantifiers after the answer); the term Z̄-group is not defined in the statement or in Mathlib/the repo — it is Kurosh's class of generalized nilpotent groups defined via central systems (Kurosh, Theory of Groups, ch. XV; Kemkhadze's papers on Z̄-groups), so the formalizer must supply that definition faithfully in the problem file.
claims.reviewer_why: c05 states Kurosh's Z̄-group faithfully: every invariant system (complete chain of G-normal subgroups containing 1 and G, closed under unions/intersections) is contained in a central system (every jump A<B has ⁅B,⊤⁆ ≤ A, i.e. B/A ≤ Z(G/A)); the theorem is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsZBarGroup G → ∀ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal → IsZBarGroup N` with answer(True) = closed under normal subgroups. Final file = c05's definitions and test lemma, plus c08's API lemmas ({⊥,⊤} is an invariant system; Z̄ ⇒ Z) with c01's non-shadowing name `IsZGroupKurosh` (c08's `IsZGroup` shadows Mathlib's unrelated `IsZGroup`). c01/c08 are mathematically equivalent to c05 and would also have been acceptable. c03/c04/c06/c07 define Z̄ as 'has a central system' — that is Kurosh's Z-group, a class closed under all subgroups, so the formalized question would be trivially true and not the open problem. c02's 'every nontrivial normal subgroup meets the centre nontrivially' is not Kurosh's class (not via central systems; contains e.g. SL(2,5), excludes free groups), so it is unfaithful.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.16

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

Is the class of all $\overline{Z}$-groups closed under taking normal subgroups?

The class of $\overline{Z}$-groups is one of Kurosh's classes of generalized nilpotent
groups, defined via systems of subgroups. A *system* of subgroups of a group $G$ is a set
of subgroups of $G$ that contains $E$ and $G$, is linearly ordered by inclusion, and is
complete (closed under unions and intersections of its subfamilies). A *jump* of the system
is a pair $A \subset B$ of members with no member strictly between them; $B/A$ is the
corresponding *factor* of the system. A system is *invariant* if all of its members are
normal in $G$, and it is *central* if it is invariant and every factor $B/A$ is central,
i.e. $B/A \subseteq Z(G/A)$, equivalently $[B, G] \subseteq A$. A system $\mathfrak{B}$
*refines* a system $\mathfrak{A}$ if $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{B}$.

A group $G$ is a *$Z$-group* if it possesses a central system, and a *$\overline{Z}$-group*
if every invariant system of $G$ can be refined to a central system of $G$. Groups with an
ascending central series ($ZA$-groups, i.e. hypercentral groups) are $\overline{Z}$-groups,
and $\overline{Z}$-groups are $Z$-groups. Kurosh's $Z$-groups are unrelated to Mathlib's
`IsZGroup` (finite groups with cyclic Sylow subgroups).

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 8.16
* A. G. Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, Vol. II, Chapter XV, § 62 (Generalized nilpotent
  groups); the notions of normal, invariant and central systems and their refinements are
  introduced in Chapter XIV, § 56.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.16»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- An *invariant system* of a group $G$ (Kurosh): a set $\mathfrak{A}$ of normal subgroups
of $G$ that contains the trivial subgroup and $G$, is linearly ordered by inclusion, and is
complete, i.e. contains the union and the intersection of every nonempty subfamily. -/
structure IsInvariantSystem (𝒜 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  normal : ∀ A ∈ 𝒜, A.Normal
  bot_mem : ⊥ ∈ 𝒜
  top_mem : ⊤ ∈ 𝒜
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝒜
  sSup_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝒜, S.Nonempty → sSup S ∈ 𝒜
  sInf_mem : ∀ S ⊆ 𝒜, S.Nonempty → sInf S ∈ 𝒜

/-- The pair $A \subset B$ is a *jump* of the system $\mathfrak{A}$: both are members of
$\mathfrak{A}$, $A$ is properly contained in $B$, and no member of $\mathfrak{A}$ lies
strictly between them. The quotient $B/A$ is the corresponding *factor* of the system. -/
def IsJump (𝒜 : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ 𝒜 ∧ B ∈ 𝒜 ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ 𝒜, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)

/-- A *central system* of a group $G$ (Kurosh): an invariant system all of whose factors are
central, i.e. for every jump $A \subset B$ the factor $B/A$ lies in the centre of $G/A$,
equivalently $[B, G] \subseteq A$. -/
structure IsCentralSystem (𝒜 : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop
    extends IsInvariantSystem 𝒜 where
  central : ∀ A B, IsJump 𝒜 A B → ⁅B, (⊤ : Subgroup G)⁆ ≤ A

/-- A group $G$ is a *$Z$-group* in the sense of Kurosh if it possesses a central system.
This is unrelated to Mathlib's `IsZGroup`. -/
def IsZGroupKurosh (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝒞 : Set (Subgroup G), IsCentralSystem 𝒞

/-- A group $G$ is a *$\overline{Z}$-group* (Kurosh) if every invariant system of $G$ can be
refined to a central system of $G$, i.e. is contained in some central system of $G$. -/
def IsZBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ 𝒜 : Set (Subgroup G), IsInvariantSystem 𝒜 → ∃ 𝒞, 𝒜 ⊆ 𝒞 ∧ IsCentralSystem 𝒞

/-- The system $\{E, G\}$ is an invariant system of $G$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isInvariantSystem_pair : IsInvariantSystem ({⊥, ⊤} : Set (Subgroup G)) where
  normal A hA := by
    rcases hA with rfl | rfl <;> infer_instance
  bot_mem := by simp
  top_mem := by simp
  isChain := IsChain.pair bot_le
  sSup_mem S hS _ := by
    by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ S
    · simp [top_unique (le_sSup h)]
    · have : sSup S = ⊥ := sSup_eq_bot.mpr fun a ha => by
        rcases hS ha with rfl | rfl
        · rfl
        · exact absurd ha h
      simp [this]
  sInf_mem S hS _ := by
    by_cases h : ⊥ ∈ S
    · simp [bot_unique (sInf_le h)]
    · have : sInf S = ⊤ := sInf_eq_top.mpr fun a ha => by
        rcases hS ha with rfl | rfl
        · exact absurd ha h
        · rfl
      simp [this]

/-- Every $\overline{Z}$-group is a $Z$-group: refine the invariant system $\{E, G\}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsZBarGroup.isZGroupKurosh (h : IsZBarGroup G) : IsZGroupKurosh G :=
  let ⟨𝒞, _, h𝒞⟩ := h _ isInvariantSystem_pair
  ⟨𝒞, h𝒞⟩

/-- In an abelian group every invariant system is already central, so every abelian group
is a $\overline{Z}$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isZBarGroup_of_commGroup (H : Type*) [CommGroup H] : IsZBarGroup H := by
  intro 𝒜 h𝒜
  refine ⟨𝒜, le_rfl, h𝒜, fun A _ _ => Subgroup.commutator_le.mpr fun g _ h _ => ?_⟩
  rw [commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (mul_comm g h)]
  exact A.one_mem

/--
Is the class of all $\overline{Z}$-groups closed under taking normal subgroups? That is, is
every normal subgroup of a $\overline{Z}$-group again a $\overline{Z}$-group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsZBarGroup G → ∀ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal → IsZBarGroup N := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.16»

items: The term Z̄-group is not defined in the notebook; I used Kurosh's definition (Theory of Groups, Vol. II, §62): G is a Z̄-group iff every invariant system of G can be refined to a central system. Reviewers should confirm against Kurosh that the class is defined via *invariant* systems (all members normal in G), not via arbitrary *normal* systems (each member normal only in the next) — since central systems are automatically invariant, the invariant-system reading is the natural one and is the one I used, but I could not consult the book offline.

A system of subgroups is modelled as `𝒜 : Set (Subgroup G)` with ⊥ ∈ 𝒜, ⊤ ∈ 𝒜, `IsChain (· ≤ ·) 𝒜`, and closure under `sSup`/`sInf` of nonempty subfamilies (Kurosh's completeness: unions and intersections of subfamilies; for a chain of subgroups `sSup` is the union).
A jump is a pair A < B of members with no member strictly between (explicit definition `IsJump` rather than `CovBy` on the subtype, for readability).
Centrality of a factor B/A (i.e. B/A ≤ Z(G/A)) is encoded as `⁅B, (⊤ : Subgroup G)⁆ ≤ A` using Mathlib's subgroup commutator.
Refinement of 𝒜 by 𝒞 is encoded as `𝒜 ⊆ 𝒞`, as in Kurosh.

Normal subgroups are quantified as `N : Subgroup G` with `N.Normal`, and the Z̄ property of N is asserted for the coerced group `↥N`; the ambient group is quantified over `Type` (repository convention in Kourovka files).

An extra `@[category test]` lemma (every abelian group is a Z̄-group) with a short proof was added to exercise the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING's request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity: the notebook does not define Z̄-group; none of the candidates (nor I) could consult Kurosh's text offline, so the definition was reconstructed from Kurosh, Theory of Groups Vol. II §56/§62: a Z̄-group is a group every invariant system of which can be refined to a central system (equivalently, all factor groups are Z-groups — I verified this equivalence: intersecting a central system of G/A with B yields a central system between A and B, and the union over jumps of an invariant system is complete). This is the main residual risk in the confidence number. Verdict on the rival readings: c02's objection that 'groups with a central system' (Z-groups) are closed under all subgroups is correct and is exactly why c03/c04/c06/c07 are unfaithful (their statement is trivially true), but c02's own centre-intersection class is not Kurosh's Z̄ class. Encoding checks done: for nonempty chains of subgroups `sSup`/`sInf` are the set-theoretic union/intersection (verified in Lean via `Subgroup.coe_iSup_of_directed`), so 'complete' is faithful; `⁅B, ⊤⁆ ≤ A` is B/A ≤ Z(G/A) by `Subgroup.commutator_le`; refinement is set inclusion as in Kurosh; the trivial group is a Z̄-group; the empty set is not a system (⊥ ∈ 𝒜 required). Quantifying over `G : Type` follows the existing Kourovka files (1_40). Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning and passes `lake --wfail build` when placed in FormalConjectures/Kourovka/ (temporary copy removed afterwards).
